paper_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What is the peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) achieved by all-polymer solar cells using the PTB7-Th:NDP-V blend, and how does it compare to the average value?
qa_pairs.answer: The all-polymer solar cell based on the PTB7-Th:NDP-V blend achieved a record-high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 8.59%, with a reported average PCE of 8.48%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: How does the molecular design of NDP-V reduce conformational disorder compared to standard PDI-vinylene backbones?
qa_pairs.answer: NDP-V reduces conformational disorder by covalently fusing half of the vinylene linkers to the bay regions of adjacent perylenediimide (PDI) units on both sides. This creates larger, shape-persistent naphthodiperylenetetraimide (NDP) units within a poly(NDP-vinylene) backbone, which limits structural flexibility.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What are the specific photovoltaic parameters (Voc, Jsc, and FF) for the optimized PTB7-Th:NDP-V device?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimized PTB7-Th:NDP-V device exhibits an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.74 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 17.07 mA cm⁻², and a fill factor (FF) of 0.67.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Explain why the HOMO level of NDP-V is lower than that of the PDI-V polymer.
qa_pairs.answer: The HOMO level of NDP-V (-5.94 eV) is lowered by 0.17 eV relative to PDI-V because the partially locked backbone of NDP-V reduces the density of the electron-donating vinylene units in the main polymer chain.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Compare the electron mobility and charge carrier balance of NDP-V and PDI-V in their respective polymer solar cell blends.
qa_pairs.answer: NDP-V exhibits a higher neat-film electron mobility of 2.5 x 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ compared to 1.9 x 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ for PDI-V. Furthermore, the PTB7-Th:NDP-V blend shows more balanced charge transport with a hole-to-electron mobility ratio (μh/μe) of 3.3, which is lower (more balanced) than the 3.8 ratio observed for PTB7-Th:PDI-V.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: What processing conditions and solvent are required to achieve high performance in NDP-V based all-polymer solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: High-performance NDP-V based devices are processed using chlorobenzene (CB) as the solvent. Notably, these devices do not require any solvent additives or post-treatments, such as thermal annealing, to reach their peak efficiencies.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: Based on GIWAXS characterization, what is the preferential molecular orientation of the PTB7-Th:NDP-V blend film?
qa_pairs.answer: The PTB7-Th:NDP-V blend film exhibits a preferential face-on orientation. This is evidenced by the observation of (100) diffraction peaks in the in-plane (IP) direction and (010) peaks in the out-of-plane (OOP) direction.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor

qa_pairs.question: How do the optical bandgap and absorption characteristics of NDP-V contribute to its performance when paired with the donor PTB7-Th?
qa_pairs.answer: NDP-V has an optical bandgap of 1.91 eV and shows significantly enhanced absorption at 402 nm and 547 nm compared to PDI-V. These enhanced absorption peaks provide a better spectral complement to the PTB7-Th donor, improving the overall light-harvesting capability of the blend.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improved Performance of All-Polymer Solar Cells Enabled by Naphthodiperylenetetraimide-Based Polymer Acceptor
